deliverable: A source-grounded comparison of two short KV Cache explainers covering what is cached, why decode gets faster, how cache memory is sized, and where the pages' coverage and labels diverge, with chapter-level citations.

turns.text: Using only these two pages, explain what a KV Cache stores and why generation gets faster with it. Compare how each page frames the cost of producing tokens — page one splits prefill and decode, page two walks the per-token inference steps — and cite the chapter heading each claim comes from (for example kvcache的原理, 缓存内容的解释, KVCache的作用, KVCache的好处).

Focus on memory. What does each page say the cache size depends on, and what concrete model or figure does either page give? Cite kvcache的显存占用 on page one and KVCache的计算 on page two, and attribute any number to that page only; do not present it as a general benchmark.

Compare reduction and limits. Which structures does page one name for cutting cache memory, and what limitations does it list? Does page two discuss reduction or limits at all? List the gaps between the pages and any place where a page's naming or characterization is internally inconsistent, citing the headings; if a page is silent, say so rather than importing outside knowledge.

authority_anchors.supports: The vLLM PagedAttention paper establishes that KV-cache memory is a dominant cost in LLM serving and is managed in blocks, an independent reference for judging the pages' statements that the cache consumes GPU memory and constrains how many requests can run.
